q: 71. Load carrying capacity of fixed beam is
options: greater than simply supported beam and cantilever beam
explain: A fixed beam has a higher degree of redundancy and smaller maximum bending moments compared to simply supported or cantilever beams for the same span and loading, allowing it to carry more load.

q: 72. The difference in placing the end of a beam simply over a support and the supporting end through a hinge on rollers is that the roller support
options: can offer reaction in the plane of rollers
will not allowed the end to lift up the deflection
will not offer reaction normal to the plane of rollers
explain: A roller support allows horizontal movement and rotation but constrains vertical movement; however, in standard civil engineering contexts, it prevents the beam from lifting off the support surface.

q: 73. The number of reaction components possible at a hinged end for a general loading is
explain: A hinged (pinned) support prevents translation in both horizontal and vertical directions, resulting in two reaction components, but it does not resist rotation.

q: 74. At either ends of plane frame, maximum number of possible transverse shear forces, are
explain: In a 2D plane frame member, there is typically only one transverse shear force acting perpendicular to the axis of the member at any given section.

q: 75. At either ends of plane frame, maximum number of possible bending moment, are
explain: According to the provided answer key, the value is zero; this typically refers to idealized hinged or pinned connections at the ends of a frame where no moment is transferred.

q: 76. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load, w. The maximum shear force, V is
explain: For a simply supported beam with UDL, the total load is wL. This is distributed equally to both supports, making the maximum shear force at the supports V = wL/2.

q: 77. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load, w. The maximum bending moment, M is
explain: The maximum bending moment for a simply supported beam with a UDL occurs at the center and is calculated as M = wL²/8.

q: 78. A simply supported beam of span L carries two equal concentrated loads, W at a distance of L/3 from either support. The maximum bending moment, M is
explain: The reaction at each support is W. The maximum moment occurs between the two loads and is equal to Reaction × Distance = W × (L/3).

q: 79. A beam is hinged at both ends and loaded with a triangular load having maximum intensity (W) at centre. Find the maximum bending moment & shear force
explain: For a triangular load (reaching peak W at center) on a simply supported span L, the total load is WL/2, the reactions are WL/4, and the peak moment at the center is WL²/12.

q: 80. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, having no external load is
explain: When there is no external load (only point loads or moments at ends), the shear force is constant and the bending moment varies linearly.

q: 81. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly distributed load is
explain: The bending moment is the integral of the shear force. For a UDL, the shear force is linear, so the bending moment diagram follows a second-degree (parabolic) curve.

q: 82. In any beam, there is acting uniformly moment then its curve is
explain: The key indicates 'parabolic arch', though pure bending (constant moment) typically results in a circular elastic curve; however, in the context of load diagrams, 'parabolic' is often associated with distributed forces.

q: 83. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly increasing load is
explain: A uniformly increasing load (triangular) results in a parabolic shear force (2nd degree) and a cubical bending moment diagram (3rd degree).

q: 84. The maximum bending moment due to moving load on a simply supported beam occurs
explain: For a single moving point load on a simply supported beam, the maximum bending moment always occurs directly under the load position.

q: 85. For a simply supported beam with a central load, the bending moment is
explain: With a central point load, the bending moment increases linearly from zero at the supports to a maximum value of WL/4 at the center.

q: 86. For a cantilever with a uniformly distributed load, w over its entire length L, the maximum bending moment is
explain: The total load is wL acting at a distance L/2 from the fixed support. Thus, M = (wL) * (L/2) = wL²/2 at the fixed end.

q: 87. The maximum deflection in the cantilever beam carrying a point load (W) at end is
explain: Standard structural formula for a cantilever with a point load at the free end: δ = WL³ / 3EI.

q: 88. In a cantilever beam a point load is applied at the free end. Which one is correct?
options: SF is uniform throughout the beam
SF varies linearly from free end to fixed end
BM is uniform throughout the beam
explain: Since there is only one load at the end and no other loads, the shear force remains constant (uniform) at value W across the entire length.

q: 89. Which of the following end conditions permits the displacement in any direction and also rotation
explain: A free end (like the tip of a cantilever) provides no restraint, allowing both translation (displacement) and rotation.

q: 90. Which of the following section is the most efficient in carrying bending moments?
explain: An I-section is most efficient because most of its area is located in the flanges, far from the neutral axis, providing a high Section Modulus (Z) for a given area.

q: 91. In an I-section almost all the shear force is taken by
explain: While flanges resist most of the bending moment, the vertical web of an I-beam resists the vast majority (usually over 90%) of the shear force.

q: 92. The bending moment is maximum on a section where shear force
explain: Mathematically, dM/dx = V. When the shear force (V) is zero or changes sign, the derivative of the moment is zero, indicating a local maximum or minimum.

q: 93. In a continuous bending moment curve the point where its changes sign is called
explain: The point where the bending moment changes sign (from sagging to hogging or vice versa) is known by all these terms in structural engineering.

q: 94. For any types of loading, the no. of point of contraflexture in a simply supported beam is
explain: In a simply supported beam, the bending moment usually maintains the same sign (sagging) throughout the span, so there are zero points of contraflexure.

q: 95. The moment diagram for a cantilever carrying concentrated load at its free end will be
explain: The moment varies linearly from 0 at the free end to WL at the fixed end, creating a triangular shape.

q: 96. Shear force for a cantilever carrying a uniformly distributed load over its whole length is
explain: The shear force varies linearly from 0 at the free end to wL at the fixed end, resulting in a triangular Shear Force Diagram.

q: 97. When a rectangular beam is loaded longitudinally, shear develops
explain: Longitudinal loading (axial) typically creates uniform stress, but internal shear can be considered present across horizontal planes depending on the distribution of load.

q: 98. When a rectangular beam is loaded transversely, the maximum compressive force develops on
explain: For a simply supported beam under transverse load, sagging occurs, which puts the top fibers in compression and the bottom fibers in tension.

q: 99. If the shear force along a section of a beam is zero, the bending moment at the section is
explain: As dM/dx = V, if V=0, the bending moment is at a stationary point, which is typically the maximum (or minimum) value in the region.

q: 100. The moments in the arch will be zero, if
options: the arch axis coincides with the line of thrust
the arch axis is parallel to the line of thrust
explain: Bending moment in an arch is the product of the thrust and the eccentricity. If the arch axis coincides with the line of thrust, the eccentricity is zero, and thus the moment is zero.

q: 101. The arch meant for supporting uniformly distributed loads, to avoid any bending moment must be
explain: A parabolic arch is the 'funicular' shape for a uniformly distributed load, meaning it carries the load purely through compression with zero bending moment.

q: 102. In any determinate structure, vertical load fall on the
explain: Determinate structures can have various support types (hinges, rollers) that receive and transfer vertical loads to the foundation.

q: 103. Three hinged arch is a .....structure.
explain: A three-hinged arch has 4 reaction components and 4 equilibrium equations (3 standard + 1 moment equation at the internal hinge), making it statically determinate.

q: 104. Three hinged arch will have three hinges
options: two at the two ends and one any where in between the two ends
two at the two ends and one at the crown only
one hinge at the crown essentially and the other two any where
explain: A standard three-hinged arch features two hinges at the supports (abutments) and a third hinge at the highest point, known as the crown.

q: 105. The value of horizontal thrust produced in a arch is
explain: For a three-hinged parabolic arch carrying a UDL (w) over the entire span (L) with rise (h), the horizontal thrust H = wL²/8h.

q: 106. The amount of bending moment induced in a cable is
explain: A perfectly flexible cable cannot resist bending; it carries loads through pure tension.

q: 107. A suspension cable, supporting loads will be under
explain: Due to their flexibility, cables adapt their shape (catenary or parabola) to remain in pure tension.

q: 108. The maximum tension in a cable occurs
options: at the highest point in the cable
at the lowest point in the cable
at the centre point of the cable
at all points in the cable
explain: Tension is the vector sum of horizontal thrust and vertical shear; since vertical shear is highest at the supports (highest points), the tension is maximum there.

q: 109. A cable subjected to UDL over its entire span assumes a shape of
explain: as per key c A cable under a uniformly distributed load (UDL) acting over the horizontal projection takes a parabolic shape.

q: 110. What is the maximum number of unknown reaction components that can be determined using only statics
explain: For a 2D structure, there are three equations of static equilibrium: ΣFx = 0, ΣFy = 0, and ΣM = 0.

q: 111. A statically indeterminate structure is the one which
options: cannot be analysed using the equations of statics alone
is not stable for general loading
can be analysed with the equations of statics alone
explain: Statically indeterminate structures have more unknowns than available equilibrium equations and require compatibility equations for analysis.

q: 112. A roller support for a space structure
options: permits the movement perpendicular to the base of the supports only
permits movement in any direction in the plane of the base
does not permit any movement but permits rotation
permits movement in any direction in the plane of the base but does not permit any rotation
explain: A roller support allows movement parallel to the supporting surface (the plane of the base).

q: 113. A hinged support for a space structure
options: permits the movement perpendicular to the base of the support only
permits movement in any direction in the plane of the base
does not permit any movement at all but permits rotation about all three mutually perpendicular axes through the joint
does not permit movement as well as rotation in any direction
explain: A hinged (pin) support restricts all translational movement but allows the members to rotate freely about the axes.

q: 114. A fixed support for a space structure
options: permits the translation only in all directions
permits rotation only about all three mutually perpendicular axes through the joint
permits rotation about all three mutually perpendicular axes and movement in any direction in the plane of the base
permits neither rotation about nor translation along, any of the three principal axes
explain: A fixed support provides total restraint, preventing both translation and rotation in all three dimensions.

q: 115. Free body diagram is
options: the diagram of the body or a part of the body in isolated equilibrium
the diagram of a body freed from all the forces that have been acting
the diagram of a body with no supports at all
explain: A Free Body Diagram (FBD) isolates a body or segment to show all active forces and reactive components acting on it.

q: 116. The free body diagram of a portion of a body will be in equilibrium under the action of
options: only external loading acting on that part without consideration of support reactions
all super-imposed loads, self-weight, support reactions, if any, and the internal reactions exposed at the cuts
only support reactions and the internal reactions exposed at the cuts
external loading acting on that part and internal reactions exposed at the cuts
explain: For any portion of a structure to be in equilibrium, all forces (external, gravity, and internal forces at the cut section) must be accounted for.

q: 117. The analysis of a structure is
options: deciding the material of the member
deciding the dimensions of the member
calculating the magnitude and nature of various straining actions at salient points of the structure
explain: Structural analysis is the process of determining the effects of loads (internal forces like shear and moment) on physical structures.

q: 118. The design of a structure is
options: the calculation of straining actions at salient points
deciding the material and proportions of the various members of the structure
explain: Design involves selecting materials and determining member sizes to ensure the structure can safely resist the analyzed forces.

q: 119. The statically indeterminate structure can be solved by
options: ignoring all deformations and assuming the structure to be rigid
using the equations of statics and the necessary number of equations of compatibility
explain: Indeterminate structures require both equilibrium equations (statics) and displacement-based equations (compatibility) to be fully solved.

q: 120. The equations of compatibility are written based on
options: the geometry of the deformed structure under the action of several forces acting
explain: Compatibility equations ensure that the deformed shape of the structure is geometrically continuous and consistent with the supports.

q: 121. A plane structure is structure
options: the various members of which lie in a plane
the thickness of various members of which will be very small
in which there will not be any bending moment
explain: A plane structure is defined as a two-dimensional structure where all members and applied forces lie within the same single plane.

q: 122. A one dimensional structure is one in which
options: one dimension is very small and other two are large
one dimension is much larger than the other two dimensions
all the three dimensions are equal
explain: In structural engineering, members like beams or columns are considered one-dimensional (line elements) because their length is significantly greater than their cross-sectional width and depth.

q: 123. A two dimensional structure is one in which
options: two dimensions are very much larger than the third
two dimensions are very much smaller than the third
explain: Two-dimensional structures, such as plates or shells, have two primary dimensions (length and width) that are much larger than the thickness.

q: 124. A plane structure which subjected to a force lying outside the plane will be
explain: If a structure designed only for in-plane forces is subjected to out-of-plane forces, it lacks the necessary constraints to resist that movement, making it unstable in that direction.

q: 125. An externally indeterminate structure is the one in which
options: the total number of external reaction components is more than the equations of statics applicable to the structure as a whole
the total number of external reaction components is more than the degree of indeterminacy
the sum of external reaction components and the degree of internal redundancy is greater than three
explain: External indeterminacy occurs when the number of support reactions exceeds the available static equilibrium equations ($$\Sigma F_x=0, \Sigma F_y=0, \Sigma M=0$$).

q: 126. An internally indeterminate structure
options: may be an unstable structure based on supports
explain: Internal indeterminacy refers to the redundancy of internal members. Per the provided key, it is categorized here as being associated with an externally determinate setup.

q: 127. A frame is completely analysed, when
options: the variation in shear is found throughout the frame
the variation in direct stress, shear and moment is found throughout the frame
the shear and moment reaction from member to member are known at every joint
explain: Complete analysis of a frame requires determining all internal actions, including axial (direct) stress, shear force, and bending moments across all members.

q: 128. A prop is
options: An additional support provided to a stable structure to avoid any displacement at the desired point in a direction perpendicular to the plane of the prop
the support which gives the maximum number of reactions for the stability of the structure
a support which will not affect the geometry of the deformed structure
a dummy support provided for architectural purposes
explain: A prop is a redundant support (often a roller or hinge) added to a structure to reduce deflection or provide extra stability at a specific point.

q: 129. A rigid prop is one which
options: permits 50% of free deflection, that would have occurred if the prop were not there
does not permit any displacement perpendicular to that plane of prop
supports the entire load and relieves all other supports completely
explain: A rigid prop acts as an unyielding support, meaning the vertical displacement (deflection) at the point of the prop is forced to be zero.

q: 130. An elastic prop is one which
options: supports the entire load and relieves all other supports completely
develops reaction proportional to the compression in itself
explain: An elastic prop (like a spring) provides a reaction force that is proportional to its deformation, following Hooke's Law ($$F = kx$$).

q: 131. A sinking prop is one which
options: does not permit any deflection at all
is provided below the level of regular supports and becomes effective after the respective deflection occurs
explain: A sinking prop refers to a support that undergoes a predetermined settlement or only engages once the structure has deflected to a certain point.

q: 132. A support over which the real beam is continuous will correspond to
options: an internal hinge in the conjugate beam
a hinged support in the conjugate beam
a fixed support in the conjugate beam
a discontinuity in the conjugate beam
explain: In the conjugate beam method, an internal support in the real beam (where slope exists but deflection is zero) corresponds to an internal hinge in the conjugate beam.

q: 133. The displacements of joints of a truss can be obtained directly from
explain: The Williot-Mohr diagram is a graphical method used to find the resultant displacement of all joints in a truss due to member deformations.

q: 134. The basic form of a pin jointed frame is
explain: The triangle is the simplest and only inherently stable geometric shape for a pin-jointed frame; other shapes require bracing to prevent collapse.

q: 135. In a pin jointed plane frame all the loads are assumed to act
options: in the plane of the frame
perpendicular to the plane of the frame
in a plane inclined at 45 degrees to the plane of the frame
explain: In the analysis of plane trusses, it is a fundamental assumption that all applied loads and reactions act within the plane of the structure.

q: 136. A pin jointed plane frame with J number of joints and n, number of members will be internally redundant, if
explain: A truss is internally redundant (over-stiff) if the number of members (n) is greater than the minimum required for stability, which is given by the formula $$n = 2j - 3$$.

q: 137. A pin jointed frame with with J number of joints and n, number of members will be a perfect frame if
explain: A perfect (just-rigid) plane frame satisfies the condition $$n = 2j - 3$$, where it is stable and determinate.

q: 138. Find the DSI of propped cantilever beam
explain: A propped cantilever has 4 reaction components (3 at fixed end + 1 at prop). With 3 equilibrium equations, the Degree of Static Indeterminacy (DSI) is $$4 - 3 = 1$$.

q: 139. DSI of structure depends upon
explain: DSI is a geometric property determined by the arrangement of members and the types of joints (rigid vs. pinned) and supports.

q: 140. The ends of continuous beam should be
explain: The end of a continuous beam can be configured in various ways—fixed, pinned, roller, or cantilever—depending on the design requirements.
